response_a:

Sweet Potato Chips

3 lbs. sweet potatoes, washed & scrubbed

1 T. oil, divided

1/2 t. salt, divided

1. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

2. Cut each sweet potato into six long, 1/4-inch-thick, slices. Pat dry or twist to remove the moisture, then brush lightly with 1/2 tablespoon of oil.

3. Working in batches, arrange the slices in oil-coated rows on the prepared baking sheets. Sprinkle lightly with 1/4 teaspoon of salt.

4. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, turning the slices over once halfway through, until the chips are tender and lightly browned.

Variation: Balsamic & Dried-Cherry Sweet Potato Chips: Sprinkle strips of sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon black pepper and 1/2 cup dried cherries before baking. When the chips are finished baking, brine with 3/4 cup balsamic vinegar. Bake for an additional five minutes to heat.

You can do a lot of damage with a DDoS attack. The FBI has expressed concerns that these attacks can be used as a form of “cyber-extortion”: an attacker may target and attack a certain website in order to get the website to pay a ransom to stop the attack. Because these attacks take a lot of computing power, DDoS attackers often target and target numerous other sites at the same time, stealing resources, bandwidth, and electricity from other people in the process. DDoS attacks can be done intentionally maliciously, but they can also be carried out accidentally: having many computers or networked devices connected to the internet at once makes it possible for a few of them to be accidentally infected with malware and be used in a DDoS attack against a target system, without the owner even knowing or intending the attack. context.speaker: assistant
context.text:
The OSI model is a conceptual framework that classifies different functionalities of network communication. This model consists of 7 layers, which are detailed below:
- Physical Layer: This layer deals with the physical aspects of a communication network, including the network hardware and cabling, as well as the actual transmission of raw bits across a connection.
- Data Link Layer: This layer connects individual network devices together to form larger network topologies, using data frames to encapsulate raw data bits for transmission across the network. The data link layer ensures reliable delivery of data frames across the network.
- Network Layer: This layer is concerned with the routing of packets across multiple networks and network devices. The network layer utilizes network addresses to create logical network paths between communicating devices, enabling the routing of packet data between devices across different networks and network segments.
- Transport Layer: The transport layer segments network data on an end-to-end basis, providing reliable data transmission between end systems, including error correction and re-transmission capabilities. This layer also creates logical connections between communicating end systems, for the purpose of maintaining a persistent communication session.
- Session Layer: The session layer manages the establishment of communication sessions between communicating end systems, providing authentication and encryption functions to secure communication sessions. This layer is also responsible for managing the synchronization of communication sessions and coordination of communication session activities.
- Presentation Layer: The presentation layer enables the translation and transformation of different data formats between communicating applications. This layer ensures the encapsulation of different data formats and media types into a common representation that can be exchanged between various network applications.
- Application Layer: This layer provides the interface for higher-level communication applications to interface with the underlying networking components and services. Additionally, this layer provides various application-oriented network services to support the communication requirements of specific applications.
